data.name: ExportVideo
data.comment: The amber command bar button that saves the project as a video file (Ctrl+E). Keep it to about 16 characters: the command bar is full at the smallest window (640 px).

data.name: ExportingButton
data.comment: The same button, dimmed, while an export runs. Keep it to about 16 characters.

data.name: Exporting
data.comment: The small caption over the file name in the export panel while the video is being written. No final period.

data.name: RunningNameFormat
data.comment: The running export's title as a screen reader names it (focus lands on it as the export starts), and what Windows lists for 10Lapse in "powercfg /requests" while the video is written. {0} the file name ("Harbor sunset.mp4"). No final period.

data.name: PercentFormat
data.comment: The large progress number. {0} the whole percent ("46"). Write it as your language writes percentages ("46 %" in French and German).

data.name: ProgressName
data.comment: The screen reader name of the export's progress bar.

data.name: GettingReady
data.comment: The time-left line before the first frame is written. Up to two lines in the 280 px panel.

data.name: EstimatingTimeLeft
data.comment: The time-left line while frames are written but the speed is not known yet. Up to two lines in the 280 px panel.

data.name: Finishing
data.comment: The time-left line once every frame is in and the video file is being completed.

data.name: TimeLeftSecondsFormat
data.comment: The time left, under a minute. {0} the seconds ("40"). Use the symbol for seconds of CoreText.Second.

data.name: TimeLeftMinutesFormat
data.comment: The time left, from a minute, on the minute. {0} the whole minutes ("2").

data.name: TimeLeftMinutesHalfFormat
data.comment: The time left, from a minute, with a half minute. {0} the whole minutes ("2" for 2 min 30 s).

data.name: FrameLabel
data.comment: The label of the export panel's row that counts frames (a frame is one picture of the video); also that row's screen reader name. Not the Frame panel (the video's shape). Keep it to about 12 characters: it shares the 280 px panel with its value.

data.name: FramesFormat
data.comment: The frame row's value: {0} the frames written, {1} all of them, both zero-padded to the same width ("0312 of 0742").

data.name: SpeedLabel
data.comment: The label of the export panel's row that says how fast the video is being written. Keep it to about 12 characters.

data.name: SpeedPhotos_one
data.comment: The speed row's value: how many photos are written each second. {0} the number with one decimal under 10 ("4.3") or none from 10 ("12"). English never shows this form: under 10 the number always has a decimal, and "1.0" takes the _other form ("1.0 photos per second"). Keep it anyway, translated. Your language's rule decides: French and Brazilian Portuguese use it for every number under 2 ("0.5", "1.5"), Spanish for "1.0"; German and Italian never show it either.

data.name: SpeedPhotos_other
data.comment: The speed row's value. {0} the number with one decimal under 10 ("4.3", "1.0") or none from 10 ("12"). It may wrap to a second line.

data.name: SpeedMeasuring
data.comment: The speed row's value before the speed is known.

data.name: OutputLabel
data.comment: The label of the export panel's row that names the video's settings (resolution, codec, quality). The same meaning as the Output panel's heading (OutputText.Heading). Keep it to about 12 characters.

data.name: OutputSummaryFormat
data.comment: The output row's value. {0} the resolution ("4K"), {1} the codec ("H.264"), {2} the quality (OutputText.QualityHigh, "High").

data.name: MinimizeHint
data.value: You can minimize 10Lapse. The export keeps going and Windows tells you when it's done.
data.comment: The hint under the export's numbers.

data.name: CancelExport
data.comment: The button that stops the export and removes the unfinished file. Keep it to about 20 characters.

data.name: RenderingFrameFormat
data.comment: The small label over the preview while the export runs. {0} the frame being written, zero-padded ("0313"). No final period.

data.name: ReadyFormat
data.comment: The finished state's title, also read by a screen reader. {0} the file name ("Harbor sunset.mp4"). No final period.

data.name: ReadySummaryFormat
data.comment: The line under the finished title. {0} the video's length ("24.7 s"), {1} the resolution ("4K"), {2} the codec ("H.264"), {3} the file size ("173 MB").

data.name: ExportedInLabel
data.comment: The label before how long the export took ("1 min 12 s"). Keep it to about 14 characters: it shares the 280 px panel with its value.

data.name: SavedToLabel
data.comment: The label before the folder the video is in ("Videos › 10Lapse"). Keep it to about 14 characters.

data.name: SavedToFormat
data.comment: The video's folder by its last two names. {0} the parent folder ("Videos"), {1} the folder ("10Lapse").

data.name: Play
data.comment: The finished state's amber button: plays the new video in the preview from its first frame (a verb). Keep it to about 12 characters; it sits beside Show in folder and the two wrap to two lines when they do not fit.

data.name: PlayName
data.comment: The screen reader name of that Play button.

data.name: ShowInFolder
data.comment: The finished state's button that opens File Explorer with the video selected. Keep it to about 20 characters.

data.name: BackToEditing
data.comment: The finished state's link back to the project's settings.

data.name: Cancelled
data.value: Export cancelled. The unfinished file was removed.
data.comment: A message bar once a cancelled export's unfinished file is gone.

data.name: CancelledFileLeft
data.value: Export cancelled. The unfinished file couldn't be removed yet, so 10Lapse removes it the next time it starts.
data.comment: A message bar when a cancelled export's unfinished file could not be removed yet.

data.name: EditsWait
data.value: The project can't change while the video exports. Wait for it to finish, or cancel the export.
data.comment: A message bar after an edit was tried during an export (a removal, a move, an import, a new project).

data.name: ImportStillRunning
data.value: Photos are still being added. Export once they're all in.
data.comment: A message bar after Export was tried while photos are still being added.

data.name: ChangedDuringDialogFormat
data.value: The export didn't start because the project or its output changed while the Save dialog was open. Choose {0} again.
data.comment: A message bar: the Save dialog was answered, but the project changed while it was open. {0} the Export button's label (ExportVideo, "Export video").

data.name: PremiereCantPlayFormat
data.value: The video was saved, but 10Lapse couldn't play it here. Open it with {0} to check it.
data.comment: A message bar: the video saved, but the preview cannot play it (a codec Windows lacks). {0} the button's label (ShowInFolder, "Show in folder").

data.name: PremiereGifFirstFrameFormat
data.value: The GIF was saved, but it's too large to play here, so the preview shows its first frame. Open it with {0} to watch it play.
data.comment: A message bar (neutral): an animated GIF over 256 MB saved, and the preview shows its first frame instead of playing it, to save memory. {0} the button's label (ShowInFolder, "Show in folder").

data.name: CloseTitle
data.comment: The title of the dialog when the window is closed during an export.

data.name: CloseMessage
data.value: The video isn't finished yet. 10Lapse stops the export and removes the unfinished file.
data.comment: That dialog's message: what closing does.

data.name: CloseConfirm
data.comment: That dialog's button that stops the export and closes the window. Keep it to about 24 characters.

data.name: CloseCancel
data.comment: That dialog's default button: keeps the window open and the export running. Keep it to about 24 characters.

data.name: FileTypeName
data.comment: The file type the Save dialog lists ("MP4 video (*.mp4)").

data.name: StartedFormat
data.comment: Read by a screen reader as the export starts. {0} the file name.

data.name: ProgressAnnouncementFormat
data.comment: Read by a screen reader at most every ten percent. {0} the whole percent ("40"), spoken, so write the word for percent.

data.name: FailedAnnouncement
data.comment: Read by a screen reader when the export fails; the message bar says why.

data.name: FinishingAnnouncement
data.comment: Read by a screen reader once every frame is written and the file is being completed.

data.name: FailedNotificationFormat
data.value: {0} couldn't be exported. Open 10Lapse to see why.
data.comment: A Windows notification when an export failed while 10Lapse was in the background. {0} the file name.

data.name: ExportKeys
data.comment: The Export button's shortcut as a screen reader names it. The letter E is fixed in code; translate only "Control", as Windows names that key on a keyboard of your language ("Strg+E" in German).
